newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bonds sag on sparse trading.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bonds sag on sparse trading.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond prices sagged on Friday on a day of very light trading activity, market players said.
"It's been a long week and most investors decided to sit (today) out," said one high-yield trader.
Despite the slowdown in selling which characterized much of the past week, traders said negative sentiment remained high throughout the corporate bond market.
Weakness in the Treasury market and the large amount of redemptions in junk bond mutual funds were likely to fuel continued investor concerns, they said.

"Whereas two months ago investors were saying 'I better buy before this paper gets tighter,' now they're saying, 'Why buy today when I can get it 5-10 basis points cheaper next month,'" said one high-grade bond trader.
Junk bond prices were down 1/2 to one point on Friday, although trading volume was low. High-grade bonds widened around five basis points on the day in light trading.
Over the past week, spreads on higher-quality investment-grade bonds widened by about about 5-10 basis points, while those of lower-quality high-grade bonds widened 5-10 basis points, traders said.
Junk bonds registered even worse losses, widening by around 22 basis points on average this week, a junk bond analyst said.
Despite the gloom, some junk players were hopeful that a late day rally in the stock market signaled that an end to the junk market's losses may be in sight.
The Dow Jones industrial average closed at 6526, rising 48.72 from yesterday's close.
"Most of what is driving this market is negative cash flow, but if equities bounce back, we might see some bottom fishers come in," said a junk bond trader.

With the dearth of investor interest, corporate bond issuers also took Friday off. A $400 million two-part high-yield offering by Triton Energy expected for Friday was postponed until next Monday, market sources said.
Strong March jobs data pushed Treasury market prices down on Friday. The benchmark 30-year Treasury closed 20/32 lower at 93-28/32. Its yield rose to 7.12 percent.
